name: Magonism
summary: Magonism is the anarcho-communist current built around Ricardo Flores Magon and the Mexican Liberal Party's Regeneracion circle, which moved from liberal opposition to the Diaz dictatorship to open war on Authority, Capital and the Church. It holds that private property, especially land, is the root of inequality, that government and the Church exist to protect it, and that workers and communities must seize land and industry and run them in common, with goods distributed by need. It drew on Kropotkin and on indigenous communal self-government, rejected electoral politics and nationalism, and sought armed social revolution under the slogan Land and Liberty.
scope: The anarchist Magonism of the Flores Magon brothers and collaborators (Ricardo, Enrique, Librado Rivera, Praxedis Guerrero) from about 1906 to Ricardo's death in 1922, based mainly on the 23 September 1911 Manifesto, The Right of Property, To Woman and To the Patriotic Proletarians. It excludes the earlier liberal phase of the 1901 Liberal Clubs and the 1906 reformist program except where noted, and the moderate Liberals who split off in 1911 (Juan Sarabia, Jesus Flores Magon). Many answers are low-confidence inferences, since the sources predate modern issues.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The 1906 program demanded a minimum wage, but the later anarchist manifesto treats wage labor itself as coercive, so adherents differ by phase.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The manifesto replaces buying and selling with distribution from a community store according to need and condemns capital as the root of inequality.

public-ownership.rationale: It wants land and industry held in common by the workers who use them, not nationalised, since the state is itself to be abolished.

unions-good.rationale: The manifesto stresses that workers must emancipate themselves, and later Magonism was carried on by trade unionists in Mexico and the US.

property-fundamental.rationale: The manifesto calls the right of individual property an iniquitous right and demands abolition of the principle of private property.

worker-ownership.rationale: The manifesto tells workers to take land, machinery and buildings and to work the land and industries in common.

strong-leader.rationale: The manifesto rejects merely swapping rulers, warning that a new governor means a new yoke.

state-harmful.rationale: Government is described as existing only to restrain the dispossessed, and the manifesto names Authority as a pillar of oppression to be fought.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: Authority is one of the supports of Capital in the manifesto, and the police and army are its enforcement arm.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

decide-locally.rationale: Magonism drew on indigenous assembly self-government and communal decision-making, and wanted no national state.

traditional-family.rationale: To Woman attacks legally enforced marriage and wives' subordination, though it also appeals to women as mothers and wives.

more-religion-public.rationale: The manifesto declares war against the Church and calls it a support of capitalist iniquity.

gender-social-construct.rationale: To Woman attributes women's subordination to tradition and law rather than nature.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Flores Magon distinguishes natural attachment to birthplace from artificial, state-taught patriotism, and has little interest in preserving national tradition as such.

gradual-change.rationale: The manifesto demands immediate expropriation without waiting for laws and calls for social revolution, not reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Workers of all nations are called friends and brothers, and borders matter less than class.

nation-first.rationale: To the patriotic proletarians denounces the bourgeois homeland and official patriotism as devices to make workers serve the rich.

open-borders.rationale: Workers across all races and nations are brothers, and the nation is described as a bourgeois construct.

revolution-justified.rationale: The manifesto calls for war against Authority, Capital and the Church and an armed expropriation.

experts-over-public.rationale: Workers must make their own emancipation; the manifesto trusts no governing elite.

central-planning.rationale: Magonism envisages free communal production and distribution, with the state abolished.

socialized-markets.rationale: Distribution is by need from a common store rather than through markets, even among worker-owned enterprises.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is to be taken from owners, not taxed, since its ownership has no moral basis.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state is to be abolished and production run by workers directly.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land and industry are worked in common, though individuals keep their house and a small plot; private holdings of productive property are rejected.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The manifesto criticizes forced wage labor and sets out common work with distribution from a community store by need.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised class partnership contradicts the open war against Capital and Authority.

one-party-rule.rationale: The manifesto opposes every government and every faction competing to govern.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Authority as such is called an unjust support of Capital, and the movement began by fighting the Diaz dictatorship.

democracy-best.rationale: The manifesto rejects electoral politics, saying political liberty benefits only place hunters, though it favours popular self-rule.

direct-votes.rationale: The indigenous assembly model Magonists admired decides matters directly in assemblies.

natural-rulers.rationale: The manifesto calls authority illegitimate and unstable and denies any right to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The manifesto endorses armed struggle against Authority, Capital and the Church.

war-builds-character.rationale: War between nations is condemned as workers dying for the property of the rich.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Liberal Party opposed clergy ties to government from 1901, and later wanted the Church abolished altogether, which entails strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Church is named a pillar of oppression and laws are regarded as made by the privileged.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Market provision of force would preserve property and capital, which the manifesto aims to abolish.

military-superiority.rationale: Magonists condemn national honor and arms as services to the rich.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Workers of all races and nations are called brothers; the nation is a bourgeois construct.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The text calls for a war of classes and sets workers against the bourgeoisie in every country; a theory of history is not spelled out.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Magonism built on indigenous communal land, assembly government and defense of communal property.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Kropotkin's mutual aid was the movement's central influence.

restore-past-order.rationale: The manifesto calls for a social revolution to build a new order, not a restoration.

direct-action.rationale: The manifesto rejects elections and parliaments and urges workers to seize land and tools directly.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The manifesto has goods distributed from a community store according to need.

production-for-use.rationale: It proposes common production to supply the community instead of private profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The manifesto describes wage labor as compelled and exploitative, with capital resting on the dispossession of workers.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The manifesto rejects any new governor or authority, even in the name of the poor.

collective-farming.rationale: Land is worked in common, echoing indigenous communal land, though each person keeps a house and plot.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Wars are portrayed as fought by workers for the property of the rich.

conscription.rationale: To Woman lists conscription among the evils taking men from families, and the movement opposed wars of states.

state-as-business.rationale: Government is nothing but an organ of capital, per the manifesto.

positive-liberty.rationale: The manifesto says political liberty does not benefit the poor, so material means are required.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Workers of every race are brothers, and no racial hierarchy is asserted.

organic-representation.rationale: The manifesto rejects representation by governors and parliaments.

total-state.rationale: The state is to be abolished.

national-rebirth.rationale: They reject national identity as a bourgeois device.

territorial-expansion.rationale: They condemn national honor and wars for property.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority of any kind is rejected.

bound-labor.rationale: Compelled labor is condemned, and the movement fought Diaz-era exploitation of workers.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers are to run production themselves, though the statement's cooperation with owners and public is milder than the manifesto's expropriation.

school-vouchers.rationale: The party sought free secular public education; vouchers for choice of school (including church ones) run against that.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy of a state is outside what the sources discuss, and a stateless programme gives no direct answer.

economic-freedom.rationale: The party held that political freedom means little without economic freedom, which is why land had to be taken.

force-without-un.rationale: They oppose wars waged by states for property.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Workers of all nations are brothers.

class-collaboration.rationale: The manifesto proclaims war against Capital, not partnership.

dominated-front.rationale: Magon opposed US economic domination of Mexico but anarchist internationalism does not favour fronts of states.

workers-nation.rationale: The text calls on workers to see each other as brothers across nations and to wage a war of classes.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: To Woman condemns laws that treat women as perpetual minors.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Workers of every race are called brothers.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The manifesto says government exists to keep the poor from going to extremes, and that laws are made by the gentry.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cross-national worker brotherhood and rejection of nationalism.

elite-replacement.rationale: Workers of all races are comrades; conspiracy narratives of this kind are absent.

national-mission.rationale: National honor is portrayed as defending the property of the rich.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: To Woman describes women as subordinated by tradition and law, paid less and legally treated as minors.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The manifesto says political liberty benefits only place hunters.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The manifesto attributes crime and misery to the system, not to inheritance.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is to be abolished, and property protection is what it exists to do.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Race divisions are rejected in favour of class unity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The manifesto speaks without distinction of sex and addresses all workers as equals.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Liberty against all impositions, including religious ones.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The 1906 program demanded compulsory, free and secular education.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The manifesto rejects any state and any new authority.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The manifesto foresees arrangements resting on the mutual consent of free individuals.

population-transfer.rationale: Workers of all races are brothers.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The manifesto endorses armed expropriation and war against Authority.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Kropotkin's mutual aid was the main influence.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Liberal Party fought for free assembly and was itself banned and persecuted.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The manifesto calls authority and capital illegitimate power over the poor.

vanguard-party.rationale: The manifesto says workers' emancipation must be the work of workers themselves.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The movement's whole aim is the interest of the dispossessed, though it rejects laws and institutions as the means.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The party supported the strikes at Cananea and Rio Blanco and workers' direct action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The manifesto roots inequality in private property.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: They reject ethnic divisions and favour worker brotherhood across races.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The movement was itself repressed under such measures.

party-controls-media.rationale: The party fought for press freedom through Regeneracion.

party-commands-army.rationale: They reject armed forces under any party or state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship barriers contradict worker brotherhood across nations.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Rejection of authority and the state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Church is an enemy, not a body to organise.

clerical-rule.rationale: Church and Authority are called supports of capital.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Flores Magon urges workers to refuse wars of the rich and wage class war; his 1918 anti-war manifesto cost him prison.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The movement fought censorship under Diaz.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources praise indigenous village life but never rank rural over urban living morally, and the movement had urban and rural bases.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The 1906 program called for secular education, and the Church is an enemy.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The manifesto says political liberty does not help the poor without expropriation.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: They reject authority and its restrictions.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The land is said to belong to all by natural law, though Magonists go further and deny private land ownership any legitimacy.

collective-defense.rationale: They oppose wars fought for the property of the rich and alliances of states.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Early Liberals sought to curb the clergy's political influence and tax Church income, though later Magonists wanted the Church abolished, not state-subordinated.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: They reject rulers and symbols of authority.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Authority and the Church are called pillars of oppression.

character-from-environment.rationale: The manifesto says crime and prostitution are products of the system, not moral failings.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Laws are said to serve the rich and authority is rejected altogether.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional government as a whole is rejected.

leader-cult.rationale: The manifesto warns against new governors; anarchists oppose cults of rulers.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Magonists never theorised a socialist state or its party leaders, as they sought to abolish the state directly.

land-redistribution.rationale: Flores Magon argues the land belongs to all and should be taken from the rich during the insurrection and worked by the people.

women-must-cover.rationale: To Woman argues against laws and religion that subordinate women.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Imperial blocs of states conflict with internationalism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The party mounted armed expeditions such as Cananea and Baja in 1911 to spark a wider rising.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The manifesto abolishes property and authority that privilege rests on.

patriotic-education.rationale: To the patriotic proletarians attacks artificial patriotism taught from childhood and calls the flag a rag.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The manifesto describes Authority as weakened and vacillating and expects collapse.

delink-world-market.rationale: Opposed foreign economic domination but anarchist internationalism has no bloc programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Workers of all nations are called brothers and all workers are exploited.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Property rights of this kind are rejected, and equality is central.

elective-rulers.rationale: They reject rulers altogether, though better than inherited rule.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The movement armed itself against Diaz, though it rejected all rulers, not just lawless ones.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Flores Magon argues no congress would expropriate land and seats go to the bosses.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity from the rich is rejected in favor of expropriation.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement was activist and revolutionary.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The manifesto says preaching patience and resignation keeps workers passive.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The manifesto links Authority, Capital and the Church and criticises the bourgeois press.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations among communist parties arise after Magon's death; the movement's own anarchism rejected party direction in any case.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Magon opposed foreign capital in Mexico but the sources give no view on foreign aid or loans as such.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous self-government is valued, but rule over others is rejected.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Fascism and communism as paired totalitarianisms is a later debate; Magon (d. 1922) died before either regime was established.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The flag is called a rag, and national symbols are dismissed.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Authority and its armed forces are enemies.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Magon opposed large American holdings, but anarchists would not rely on state blocking.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Indigenous assembly governance with rotating duties informed the movement.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private financial accumulation conflicts with common provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land belongs to all by natural law, and the manifesto lets each person hold a house and plot.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliaments are seen as controlled by the rich, but they reject the state budget too.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Magon opposed foreign holdings but would abolish private land ownership entirely.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Opposed to states' wars and domination.

corporate-influence.rationale: Magon opposed the large American economic presence in Mexico.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Law is called the creation of landholders to protect their theft, so no moral duty follows.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Class war, not ethnic conspiracy, is the framework.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: To Woman says marriage under law and economic need is a form of prostitution.

local-production.rationale: Communal production and a local store fit.

informal-organisation.rationale: The party worked through small groups and juntas.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Opposed to authority and to domination.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The manifesto has land and industries held in common, with each keeping his own house.

religion-illusion.rationale: To Woman tells people not to look to heaven for solutions, and the manifesto faults the Church's preaching of resignation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: To Woman ties women's low pay and marriage under need to the capitalist order and calls for revolution.

socialized-care.rationale: To Woman is concerned with women's economic and legal subordination but proposes no particular way of organising housework and childcare.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Baja revolt set up communes on Kropotkinist lines, and the manifesto calls for common work and distribution.

majority-settlement.rationale: Opposed to national and ethnic domination.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement was itself suppressed and demanded free assembly.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Church is an enemy and the movement fought religious impositions.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Church is an enemy and religion in politics is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Indigenous assembly democracy and workers' self-organization.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: To Woman describes women as doubly oppressed, as workers and women.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The manifesto frames politics as a war of classes.

alienated-labor.rationale: The manifesto objects that workers are compelled to hire out their labor for distasteful tasks.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority and the Church are called supports of iniquity.

social-market-economy.rationale: Markets are rejected for common ownership.

property-franchise.rationale: Congress being filled by the rich is the criticism.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist links between domination of women and nature are not found in the sources, which treat women's oppression as legal and economic.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The manifesto criticises the bourgeois press and the party relied on its own paper.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Law is seen as a class tool.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Church is rejected rather than reformed.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Concentrated capital is described as the root of oppression.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Authority supports capital, and crime is a product of the system.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Mutual aid, not charity, is the principle.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: To Woman condemns wives' legal custody by husbands.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The manifesto condemns the idle living on capital.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: To Woman addresses women as a single group; the debate over a fixed category is a modern one the sources do not touch.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Magonists honored fallen comrades, but nationalist martyrdom is rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics is a material class war.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Reform of religious texts is not Magonist territory, since the Church is opposed outright.

independent-unions.rationale: Worker self-organization without state or party control.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The emancipation of the workers is the work of workers themselves.

municipal-property.rationale: Communal property was defended in indigenous communities.

person-over-state.rationale: The state is rejected as serving the rich.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Class, not race, is the axis.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The text condemns wars fought by workers for the rich but proposes no doctrine on defensive armed forces, which they reject anyway.

native-born-offices.rationale: Office-holding restricted by birth contradicts the worker brotherhood across nations and races, and the movement rejected state office altogether.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national youth movements serve the patriotism and state loyalty that To the Patriotic Proletarians condemns as artificial and taught from childhood.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Magonists sought armed popular revolution against the state and wanted government abolished, so a state monopoly on arms is the opposite of their position.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The manifesto rejects taking power and calls for abolishing Authority, Capital and the Church through armed revolution.

sacred-nation.rationale: They rejected nationalism and patriotism as tools of the ruling class and addressed workers across borders.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: To Woman and the Manifesto call for women's equality and for property held in common, so women would hold land on the same terms as men.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Manifesto attacks the Church as a pillar of Authority and Capital, so privileging any religious interpretation in law would be rejected.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Manifesto rejects elections and government as instruments protecting private property, so rulers chosen by vote are not democratic in its sense.

premarital-sex.rationale: To Woman attacks church and legal marriage as tools of oppression, so sex outside marriage is accepted.

women-suffrage.rationale: To Woman demands women's full equality, but Magonists rejected voting and public office as bourgeois politics, so adherents would not endorse the vote as such.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: To Woman argues the Church and religion bind women to subjection alongside law and marriage.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The Right of Property says land ownership began in conquest and fraud and that land belongs to all, so ownership by first claim is rejected.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The manifesto names the Church with Capital and Authority as an oppressor, and the audit's religion answers are strongly negative.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The manifesto warns that any new government is a new yoke and calls for abolishing property and authority, so defending a state-owned economy is rejected.

national-church-status.rationale: The manifesto lists the Church as an enemy of the people, so legal privilege for a church is rejected.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Magonism rejected patriotism and the nation, holding that the land belongs to all humanity, so a national duty to protect ancestral land is opposed.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Magonists held that law and government serve the propertied and rejected state authority, so killing by the state without trial is opposed.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: To the Patriotic Proletarians rejects nationalism and the flag in favour of workers' internationalism.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Right of Property holds that land belongs to all, and that its appropriation by a few is robbery.

self-ownership.rationale: The anarchist-communist stress on liberty, and To Woman's call for women to be free of masters, support personal rights over body and labour.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Magonism rejected elections, leaders and authority alike, so it would not hold that a leader should rule through the people against parties.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The manifesto holds that government exists to protect capital and calls for its abolition, so privileges to businesses are opposed.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Magonists made war on the Church as one of the pillars of Authority, and sought the end of religious influence in public life.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: To Woman attacks marriage law as a tool of male authority and calls on women to claim freedom.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The Right of Property says property began in violence and robbery and that the land belongs to all, so wealth is unjust whatever the process.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Manifesto and The Right of Property call law the landholders' tool and urge direct expropriation, so unjust law has no claim on obedience.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: To the Patriotic Proletarians rejects patriotism and the flag as tools of the ruling class and calls for workers' internationalism.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Magonists wanted to abolish government, capital and party-led politics, rejecting both markets and state rule (Manifesto).

police-more-powers.rationale: Authority is one of the supports of Capital in the manifesto, and the police and army are its enforcement arm. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: Organised religion helps keep working people submissive to the wealthy.
missingStatements.rationale: The manifesto lists the Church with Capital and Authority and criticises its preaching of patience, resignation and humility.

missingStatements.text: Revolutionaries should abolish government rather than take power themselves.
missingStatements.rationale: The manifesto warns that a new governor is a new yoke and rejects every candidate and faction.

missingStatements.text: The land belongs to everyone, and ownership of it by a few has no moral basis.
missingStatements.rationale: The Right of Property says land ownership began in conquest, fraud and abuse of power and that the land belongs to all Mexicans by natural law.

notes: Magonism changed over time: the 1906 program was a radical-liberal reform package (minimum wage, eight-hour day, secular education), and the 1911 manifesto went to anarchist communism. Answers follow the later anarchist phase; where reformist demands bear on a statement the rationale says so. Most low answers are inferences about issues the sources never discuss.
